stem: Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) says that all human beings are "born free and equal" in what?
hints: Article 1 is about what every person has just by being human, not what a person owns, earns or learns.
Recall the first sentence of Article 1. It begins: "All human beings are born free and equal in ..."
Cross out every pair that differs from person to person, such as money, position or schooling. Pick the pair that all people share from birth.

solution.methodName: Recall the exact words of the provision

steps.action: Find the provision: Article 1 of the UDHR.
steps.why: Article 1 is the opening rule of the Declaration. The other articles build on it.

steps.action: Recall its first sentence: "All human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights."
Check the other choices. Wealth, talent, rank, power, skills and knowledge are not the same for everyone, so people cannot all be born equal in them.
steps.why: The Declaration is about what every person has just by being human.

steps.action: The answer is dignity and rights.

trapNotes.wealth and talent: People are not born with equal wealth or talent. Article 1 says all are born equal "in dignity and rights".
trapNotes.rank and power: Article 1 is not about rank or power. It says all are born equal "in dignity and rights".
trapNotes.skills and knowledge: Skills and knowledge are learned, so they differ from person to person. Article 1 says all are born equal "in dignity and rights".

sourceRef.citation: Universal Declaration of Human Rights, Article 1
